questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study abroad in a country where english is the main language. It was also important that they had a good biology department.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been a very good experience. I've learned a lot both personally and academically.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The host university have been very good to help upon arrival and have provided all the necessary informations.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Help to figure out if my courses were a good fit and did not overlap and a hole day with information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Different types of housing were available but all similar.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I could either choose to cook my own meals or get a meal plan.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: If you are only here for a semester, the easiest way to do it will be to choose to live on campus. But you can probably find cheaper places in town. Housing on campus is near the university and up the hill contrary to housing in town.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very easy to get a place on campus. But I think it has been quite expensive in proportion to what you get. The water in my house did not work properly the first 2,5 months.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a very stressfull process because it could take more than a week for people to answer on mail.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't remember the process probably but I know that you had to choose potential Universities about a year before and figure out what courses you would like and write an application.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online seminars.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up getting all three courses that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you have plenty of time to figure it all out and ask friends or others that have been on exchange to help you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Brain, behavior and psychology - first year
Cell and cancer biology - second year
Microbial Pathogenesis - third year

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At Aberystwyth you have to write assignments throughout the semester. You get feedback and the grade will be a part of your final grade. I think that is a good way to do it contrary to University of Copenhagen where your final grade only depend on an exam. At Aberystwyth University they also record all lectures so you are able to watch them again later.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Brain, behavior and psychology
Cell and cancer biology
Microbial Pathogenesis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of them. I learned a lot and they all gave good feedback on assignments.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't think I had any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The prices is kind of the same as in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds. There is something for everyone and people are very including.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined the running club at the university and it was one of the best things I did. They had sessions two times a week and a social evening in town.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to take the train or bus to places near the town or even go to the bigger cities in England for a few days.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I was very easy. People are very nice and in some ways it is like being in Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club! That's the best way to do it.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Some people speak welsh, but everyone can speak English.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very nice and openminded.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Join a club, find some exchange students to hang out with and make sure to experience the nature.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The running club. That I got to be a part of the group and met so many good people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Put myself out there and meet new people.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
